decision_points.question: which regression model / estimator is used for the primary effect?
decision_points.why_rival: each fixes a different functional form for estimating the effect (LPM/OLS, Poisson GLM, GEE, Bayesian random-intercept, inverse-variance ratio meta-regression); an analyst commits to one primary estimator

decision_points.question: how are the standard errors of the effect estimate computed?
decision_points.why_rival: each is a rival variance estimator for the same coefficient (conventional, HC1/HC3 heteroskedasticity-robust, generic/player/referee/two-way clustered, sandwich), and the ICC diagnostic just defends the player-clustered answer; only one is reported for the headline estimate

decision_points.question: how is the bootstrap resampling of the estimate performed?
decision_points.why_rival: each specifies a rival scheme for generating the bootstrap distribution (cluster vs dyad resampling, resample count, statistic refit, failure handling); an analyst runs one bootstrap design

decision_points.question: how is the p-value / test statistic derived from the estimate and its standard error?
decision_points.why_rival: each is a rival normal-approximation Wald/z construction turning an estimate and an SE into significance; one significance test is reported

decision_points.question: what overall conclusion is drawn about the hypothesis?
decision_points.why_rival: each is a rival verdict on whether the hypothesis is supported given the results; an analyst lands on one

decision_points.question: which covariate / right-hand-side specification does the model use?
decision_points.why_rival: each fixes how predictors and controls enter the model (a single blocked-entry strategy vs a set of alternative RHS specs); one specification governs the primary model

decision_points.question: which version of the source dataset is loaded?
decision_points.why_rival: settles whether the analysis starts from the raw, unfiltered dyad file

decision_points.question: what text encoding is used when reading the CSV?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the character encoding for the file read

decision_points.question: how is a player-referee pair identifier constructed?
decision_points.why_rival: settles how a unique dyad key is formed

decision_points.question: how are categorical string fields encoded as numeric IDs?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the numeric recoding of player/position/referee/country strings

decision_points.question: how is a per-player career-goals feature derived?
decision_points.why_rival: settles construction of the aggregated goals covariate

decision_points.question: how are dyad rows aggregated for description/plotting?
decision_points.why_rival: settles collapsing to one row per player for descriptive display

decision_points.question: how are dyad rows expanded to a per-game unit?
decision_points.why_rival: settles reshaping dyads into one row per game for analysis

decision_points.question: which dyad rows are included based on red-card counts?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the red-card-based row restriction of the sample

decision_points.question: how are leagues filtered/thresholded for inclusion?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the league-level size/red-card inclusion threshold

decision_points.question: what secondary confirmatory model is fit?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the additional logistic regression run alongside the primary analysis

decision_points.question: what exploratory profile/subgroup analysis is performed?
decision_points.why_rival: settles the dissimilarity-based clustering of fitted profiles into relative-risk groups
